name: Tute subastado
description: Tute subastado: auction Tute. Trump or contract determined by auction/bidding. 40-card Spanish.

overview.description: Tute subastado: auction Tute. Trump or contract determined by auction/bidding. 40-card Spanish.

history.origins: Tute originated in Italy as tutti and spread to Spain in the 19th century, becoming one of the most popular card games there. Tute subastado is the auction variant: trump is not determined by a turned card but by a round of bidding; the highest bidder becomes soloist and chooses trump, and must make at least the number of points bid.
timeline: 20th century: Tute subastado (auction Tute) documented; trump chosen by bidding; soloist bids points, opponents try to prevent making the bid.

setup.deck: Standard Spanish 40-card pack (four suits: oros, espadas, copas, bastos). In Tute subastado the twos are set aside and 36 cards are used; 12 cards are dealt to each player.

rules.objective: In each deal the highest bidder becomes soloist and chooses trumps. The soloist aims to take at least the number of points bid (from tricks, declarations, and last trick). Opponents try to prevent the soloist from making the bid. Minimum bid is 60 points in multiples of five.
rules.gameplay: After the deal there is one round of bidding (minimum 60, bids in multiples of five); the highest bidder is soloist and declares trump, then leads to the first trick. Play follows standard Tute rules: follow suit, head the trick or trump if unable to follow; soloist may declare king-horse (40 in trumps, 20 in other suits) after winning a trick. Soloist makes the contract if their total (card points, declarations, and 10 for last trick) equals or exceeds the bid.
